title: Cohort-priority fallback scheduler with adaptive holdpoints and embargo windows
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation:
This PR introduces a scheduler and control-plane primitives for prioritized cohort-based fallbacks during staged rollouts. We observed that during multi-cohort canaries a single global fallback policy either reacts too quickly (causing unnecessary rollbacks) or too slowly (allowing bad models to serve high-value cohorts). The new scheduler lets operators attach an explicit cohort priority and embargo window to holdpoints so that critical cohorts are observed with stricter gating and lower-risk cohorts can be drained or hedged.

Design summary and key features:
- Cohort priority lanes: each cohort can be assigned a numeric priority; scheduler uses priority to determine ordering of drain/traffic-shift actions when a rollback or partial fallback is triggered.
- Adaptive holdpoints: holdpoints now support a dynamic timeout that lengthens or shortens based on recent signal stability (latency/error variance). This reduces noisy premature rollbacks while keeping total rollout time bounded.
- Embargo windows: ability to declare a short embargo period after a canary step where automated rollback is suppressed unless severity threshold is exceeded — useful to let downstream async processes warm up.
- Hedged shadowing: low-priority cohorts can be routed as 'hedged-shadow' to compare outputs with minimal latency impact; we capture diff metrics and allow automatic promotion back to normal routing when confidence is high.
- Rollback scheduler: orchestrates rollback actions across cohorts using priority-aware quorums; supports graceful draining, immediate cutoff, and partial rollback (percent-based) strategies.
- Backwards-compatible API: rollout CRD/API additions are additive; existing rollout specs remain valid. A migration job updates stored rollout records to add default priority=50 and embargo=0s where unspecified.

Implementation notes:
- Control plane: new scheduler service (scheduler/priority_fallback) implemented in Go under rollout/controller. Scheduler exposes a small reconciliation loop and an evaluation engine that computes per-cohort action plans.
- Runtime hooks: lightweight runtime adapter added to route-planner to accept per-cohort routing directives (drain, hedged-shadow, redirect-percent). Changes in route-planner are confined to an adapter interface to keep the serving runtime insensitive to control-plane internal changes.
- Metrics and observability: added metrics: rollout_cohort_priority, rollback_decision_latency_seconds, embargo_suppressed_rollbacks_total, hedged_shadow_diff_rate. Dashboards updated under observability-pack/rollouts/priority-lanes.
- Safety: decision engine simulates the plan against a dry-run evaluation harness before commit; we also added a built-in kill-switch for immediate global rollback (admin-only).

Migration and rollout plan:
- Migration job: rollout/migrations/add_defaults_20241107 runs as part of the release; it sets sensible defaults for existing rollouts. The job is idempotent.
- Staged rollout of the feature: feature-flag guarded (flag: rollout.priority_fallback). Initially enabled for internal Redwood accounts and Dedicated customers under opt-in.
- Monitoring and alerting: new SLOs and alerts for embargo-suppressed rollback rates and hedged-shadow drift. Ops checklist included below.

- Security: audit of kill-switch authorized paths; RBAC rule added (rollout.admin).

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay special attention to eviction/tracking semantics in priority_scheduler.go: we use a two-phase commit to avoid inconsistent partial drain states.

review_thread: Liam O'Connor: Nice design. Can you clarify why priority is numeric instead of enum? Concern: ops may misinterpret 0-100 scales.
Priya Nair: We chose numeric to allow fine-grained ordering and future weights. Added docs/operations/rollout_priority_lanes.md with recommended sweet spots and examples (0, 25, 50, 75, 100).
Ethan Brooks: The adaptive holdpoint window math looks complex. Add more unit tests for edge cases (high variance low mean).
Priya Nair: Added tests for variance edge-cases and added a fallback to fixed-timeout if signals are insufficient.
Marta Gomez: Do we have any perf regression on route-planner when hedged-shadow is enabled?
Priya Nair: Benchmarked in perf-canary lab; hedged-shadow adds ~0.8% CPU and 2-3ms p95 tail in worst-case under synthetic load; documented in PR and dashboard notes.

Liam O'Connor: Approving after unit-test additions. Verified migration is idempotent in staging. 
(Approved)
